steps.observation: Work on this for 60 seconds; do not stop early. Explain the difference between RNA and DNA.

steps.action:
Here’s a concise summary of the main differences between RNA and DNA:

1. Sugar backbone  
   • DNA: deoxyribose (lacks an oxygen atom on the 2′ carbon)  
   • RNA: ribose (has a hydroxyl group on the 2′ carbon)  

2. Nitrogenous bases  
   • DNA: adenine (A), guanine (G), cytosine (C), thymine (T)  
   • RNA: adenine (A), guanine (G), cytosine (C), uracil (U) instead of thymine  

3. Strandedness  
   • DNA: typically double-stranded, forming a stable right-handed double helix  
   • RNA: usually single-stranded, but can fold into complex 3D structures via intra-strand base pairing  

4. Function  
   • DNA: long-term storage of genetic information; blueprint for all cellular processes  
   • RNA: multiple roles, including  
     – mRNA (messenger RNA): carries genetic code from DNA to ribosomes  
     – tRNA (transfer RNA): delivers amino acids during protein synthesis  
     – rRNA (ribosomal RNA): core component of ribosomes  
     – regulatory RNAs (e.g., miRNA, siRNA): control gene expression  
     – some catalytic RNAs (“ribozymes”)  

5. Stability and location  
   • DNA: chemically more stable (deoxyribose resists hydrolysis), primarily found in the nucleus (and mitochondria/chloroplasts)  
   • RNA: less stable (2′-OH makes it more prone to hydrolysis), synthesized in the nucleus but mostly functions in the cytoplasm (and organelles)  

6. Replication and turnover  
   • DNA: replicated by DNA polymerases before cell division; very low turnover  
   • RNA: transcribed by RNA polymerases continually; high turnover and dynamic regulation  

In short, DNA is a durable, double-stranded repository of hereditary information, while RNA is a versatile, often single-stranded molecule that plays many roles in expressing, regulating, and even catalyzing genetic functions.
